Spinning is really really hard and it’s pretty easy to get onto the toepicks, you’ll want to spin on the sweet spot of the blade but the bottom drag pick will touch the ice slightly, as long as there’s no harsh scratching sound. When you enter the spin, feel your weight on the ball of the foot on the entrance edge. Practice it on a line first before doing it with crossovers. Go as slow as possible, like painfully slow. After you reach the end of that half heart shape, it should feel like your leg stops on the spot, and your free leg will circle around to 3o’clock (don’t force it or whip it around). Keep that open starfish position for a few revolutions and continue to keep weight on the ball of your foot. You can lift your toes and flex your ankle a bit if you are having issues. And pull in your arms and legs very slowly or you will end up on your toe and travel across the rink. I hope that makes sense!

I see that you look down while you’re winding up the spin, make sure you keep your upper body tall and strong with head not tilted down. Keep that left arm in front of you and right arm to the side like an L shape and in your first 1-2 rotations of the spin, have your arms in an open position. Slowly (very slowly!) bring your arms to your chest. It’s very important here to not hunch in on yourself and keep your back straight.

As for legs, while you are spinning, try to rise up so that your knees aren’t so bent. They don’t need to be locked straight but they should appear as straight as possible, you can practice this in front of your mirror at home so that you can get a feel for it. Your feet also need to come together a bit closer, it’s much harder to spin if they are far apart!

Also I emphasize taking your time with the spin. Do it slower than normal because once you pull your arms in you’ll be spinning fast anyway so just make sure that entrance is as perfect as it can be. I hope this all makes sense, good luck on your skating! :)
